factual_claims.claim: StereoSet is a large-scale natural English dataset designed to measure stereotypical biases in four domains: gender, profession, race, and religion.
StereoSet contains 4 target domains, 321 target terms, and 16,995 test instances (triplets).
Popular pretrained language models like BERT, GPT2, RO BERTA, and XLN ET exhibit strong stereotypical biases.
People associate stereotypes with relatively more negative associations than anti-stereotypes (41% vs. 33%).
As model size increases, language modeling ability (lms) increases, and correspondingly its stereotypical score (ss).
GPT2-large is the best performing language model (88.3) followed by GPT2-medium (85.9) on the StereoSet test set.
RO BERTA-base is the least stereotypical model (50.5) among the pretrained models tested.
The Amazon Mechanical Turk population is 55% women and 45% men, with 80% of the populous under the age of 50.
The median income of workers on AMT is $47k, compared to the United States median income of $57k.

BERT-base has 110M parameters, BERT-large has 340M parameters, GPT2-small has 117M parameters, GPT2-medium has 345M parameters, GPT2-large has 774M parameters, RO BERTA-base has 125M parameters, RO BERTA-large has 355M parameters, XLN ET-base has 110M parameters, and XLN ET-large has 340M parameters.
The StereoSet dataset was validated by five validators, and only CATs where at least three validators agreed on the labels were retained.
